method: Claude's rating: crowd score weighted by review volume, plus awards and guide listings, spread onto a 5-star scale.

venues.name: Nothing within walking distance
venues.note: No food near the lock; Banagher is the next stop upstream.

venues.name: Flynn's of Banagher
venues.note: Casual, friendly gastropub in the centre of Banagher with a dog-friendly yard out the back. Generous pub meals; the steak and beef dishes and the Death by Chocolate cake are what reviewers remember. Lively when sport is on. Dinner from 17:00.

venues.name: JJ Hough's Singing Pub
venues.note: Famous singing pub with music and singing every night and a packed, lively room even on a Sunday; a great welcome from the owner. One reviewer recommends the beetroot burger, so food may now be served; ring ahead.

venues.name: Corrigan's Corner House
venues.note: Pub: drinks only, no food. Brilliant old-school pub on the corner of Main Street: pints pulled with skill, a helpful owner and trad music most weekends.

venues.name: Simon Lyons
venues.note: Pub: drinks only, no food. Old-world pub full of character, warm and cosy, run by Simon and Mary, who are much praised as hosts; great Guinness and a Wednesday night music session. Welcoming to families.

venues.name: McIntyre's Pub
venues.note: Cosy, family-run country pub where the Shannon meets the Grand Canal, with a fire, a great pint, a warm welcome and the odd play or gig. Good-value pub food when the kitchen is on: burgers, cod, chicken burgers with chips and salad. Food served at weekends from March to December; check its Facebook page for updates.

google: Luker's Bar , Restaurant & Live Music venue
venues.name: Luker's Bar
venues.note: Historic bar (est. 1757) by the bridge, a warren of rooms: an old bar full of memorabilia, a roof terrace over the river, a courtyard bar with pool table and a Big Top for gigs; The Dubliners once played. Good pub grub and a Sunday roast; live music most weekends. Its own Instagram said food seven days, 12:00–21:00, but a post of 8 Nov 2026 says food Wednesday to Sunday from 12:00; ring ahead.

venues.name: JJ Killeen's
venues.note: Famous old pub (est. 1721) with rooms, its own Seven Churches whiskey, decor that feels decades back and live music every Saturday and Sunday; family-friendly with high chairs and a kids' menu. Known for seafood chowder, huge fish and chips and a good-value full Irish. Its own Instagram (Nov 2026) says food served daily from 09:30; its winter food hours (Oct 2026) run to 19:00 Monday to Thursday, 21:00 Friday and Saturday, 20:00 Sunday. No menu online.

venues.name: Fallon's Bar
venues.note: Pub: traditional bar dating from 1846, quirky, in three different rooms, with a fine whiskey and gin selection, trad sessions and a friendly host. Now serves food with The Organic Kitchen: a small menu, well reviewed for the money; times and menu not published.

venues.area: Ballinasloe Marina (up the River Suck from Shannonbridge)

venues.name: Brewery Lane
venues.note: Cosy traditional pub and restaurant in the town centre with a balcony terrace and beer garden. Brunch, lunch and à la carte, with a new winter menu from 13 Nov 2026 (its own Instagram): juicy grilled chicken, battered cod, curry and burgers. Friendly staff; live music, comedy nights and rugby, with a party room downstairs at weekends.

venues.name: Fusion Restaurant & Takeaway
venues.note: Chinese and Malaysian restaurant and takeaway, open late for sit-down meals. Chicken satay, chow mein and a well-rated spice bag (reviews vary); generous portions at fair prices, friendly service.

google: Good Taste Chinese Restaurant and Takeaway
venues.name: Good Taste Chinese
venues.note: Chinese takeaway with a few tables. Noodle boxes are its best-liked dish; reviews of the rest are mixed.

venues.name: Bistro 18
venues.note: Daytime café with a pretty back terrace: good coffee and hearty, good-value plates such as lasagne, chicken curry from the specials, and a big veggie breakfast. Friendly staff.

venues.name: Venezia
venues.note: Italian restaurant, handy for a quick bite or a big table: creamy pastas, carbonara, cannelloni, pizza and a children's bolognese, in generous portions at fair prices, with a good wine list. Most reviewers are happy; a few found it average.

venues.name: Umi Kitchen
venues.note: Pan-Asian restaurant and takeaway: Chinese dishes, nasi goreng and Thai green curry, fresh and generous; dishes marked spicy are mild. Family-friendly sit-in with friendly staff.

venues.name: Kariba's Restaurant & Coffee House
venues.note: Cosy daytime restaurant with high ceilings and stone walls, full of locals. Home cooking: beef stroganoff, steak sandwich, salmon, sourdough sandwiches, and cakes baked on the premises (chocolate biscuit cake, coffee cake, pear and almond tart). Friendly owner and staff.

venues.name: Zaiqa (Indian)
venues.note: Small, cosy Indian restaurant with friendly staff; book, as space is tight. Butter chicken, tikka masala, chicken tikka and lamb korma are the dishes reviewers praise; halal menu.

venues.name: Coffee stand at the monastic site
venues.note: Seasonal coffee and snacks only; no restaurant within walking distance.

venues.name: @Fine, Italian Deli & Wine
venues.note: Small Neapolitan family's deli, café and wine bar, opened June 2025 and much loved: outstanding pizza and pinsa, fresh gnocchi, a generous tiramisu (orange too), affogato, pistachio desserts and proper espresso. Warm, relaxed and spotless; come hungry. It closes for a summer family holiday in August.

venues.name: Bacchus Restaurant
venues.note: Turkish-owned Mediterranean restaurant on Custume Pier by the bridge, on two floors with riverside tables. Big portions at good value: meze platters, Anatolian braised beef, seafood platters, steaks and fish specials such as kadaif-crusted monkfish.

venues.name: Beans & Leaves
venues.note: Bright, family-run riverside café and bistro, a favourite for breakfast and brunch: French toast, waffles, pancakes and big plates, with vegetarian and gluten-free well catered for. Very friendly; dog-friendly (bed, water and treats) and good with children. Tripadvisor Travellers' Choice 2026; known at Christmas for salted caramel mince pies (its own Instagram).

venues.name: Chocolate Brown Athlone
venues.note: Cosy coffee shop with old-world decor and lots of light. Excellent coffee and chai lattes, scones, sausage rolls (one reviewer's best ever), cakes and pastries; very friendly staff.

venues.name: Dead Centre Brewing
venues.note: Craft brewery taproom on the river with outdoor seating and views of the Shannon. Its own beers (red ale, IPAs, Dead Pixel lager; try a tasting flight) and hearty food: brick-oven pizza, wings, burgers, steak fries. Closed Mondays (open bank holiday Mondays from 12:30) and Tuesdays.

venues.name: Gertie Brownes Bar & Bistro
venues.note: Award-winning old-style pub and bistro by the bridge with open fires in winter: cosy, friendly and dog-friendly. Comfort food: beef stew and fish and chips are what people praise, with home-made daily specials (fishcakes, stuffed chicken), paninis and tacos at lunch, home-made desserts and cocktails. Bar food until 21:00; live music some nights (its own Instagram).

venues.name: Jalan Jalan Restaurant
venues.note: Asian restaurant on Church Street: sushi, miso soup and pan-Asian dishes. Reviews are mixed on food, service and cleanliness; some families had a good time.

venues.name: Peddler Mac's Bar & Beer Garden
venues.note: Old-world bar with lots of seating areas and a covered beer garden out the back, where a pizza truck serves wood-fired pizza (Broke Boy Pizza) Wednesday to Sunday. Live music every night except Tuesdays; quiz nights. Its menus page was not loading on 24 Nov 2026.

venues.name: Rustic Roots Restaurant
venues.note: Cosy modern-Irish restaurant by the bridge. Known for Atlantic fish chowder (in a bread bowl for €5 more), Irish stew in bread, mushroom soup and salmon; desserts praised. Service can be uneven.

venues.name: Sean's Bar
venues.note: Ireland's oldest pub, a short walk from the town quay and a must for boaters: history and artefacts on every wall, a great pint and Sean's own whiskey; lively, friendly and busy with tourists in the day. Go for the pint and the atmosphere rather than food.

venues.name: The Cellar Bistro
venues.note: Characterful bistro on Strand Street, sister to Gertie Brownes and formerly Hatter's Lane, with a broad menu: fajitas, pasta, bacon and cabbage, sea bass, now with Gertie Brownes classics. Service is much praised; book on busy evenings. Its own Instagram said open daily from July 2026; the hours shown here differ.

venues.name: The Left Bank Bistro
venues.note: Bright, buzzing bistro on the left bank near Sean's Bar, recommended among Shannon boaters. Eclectic modern menu: half duck with Asian slaw, halibut and other specials on the board, home-made desserts; good short wine list. Listed in the Michelin Guide. Lunch menu Tuesday to Friday 12:00–17:00.

venues.name: Thyme Restaurant
venues.note: Fine dining by the bridge, among the best meals in the region: Michelin Bib Gourmand, in the Sunday Times 100 Best Restaurants 2026 and Best Restaurant in Westmeath at the Irish Restaurant Awards 2026 (its own Instagram). Seasonal menus of beautifully presented dishes (lobster, guinea fowl, lamb, beef), attentive staff and good value for the standard. Book. Taste of the Waterways award 2022.

venues.name: The Snug Bar
venues.note: Pub: cosy bar by Sean's with a decorated beer garden out the back and friendly barmen who welcome visitors; pizzas served (pint-and-pizza offers) and an upstairs room for groups.

venues.name: Al Mezza (Lebanese)
venues.note: Lebanese restaurant with distinctive decor: shawarma, skewers, sharing platters and curry. Reviews are sharply divided on quality and portion size.

venues.name: Bastion Kitchen
venues.note: Small, cosy café near the river, popular for breakfast and lunch with organic produce: smashed avocado toast with poached eggs, good coffee and teas. Get there early for lunch. Open Monday to Saturday for sit-in and takeaway.

venues.name: Craft Bistro
venues.note: Big, busy daytime café on Church Street with plenty of seating: breakfast served all day (fry, pancakes), huge triple-decker club sandwiches, chicken pesto toasties, monthly special sandwiches, fries and waffles at good prices; quick, friendly service.

venues.name: Il Colosseo
venues.note: Popular Italian restaurant just off the main street: pizza (with burrata), pasta such as carbonara and creamy fettuccine, good desserts and red wine at reasonable prices; friendly, fast service. Often full, even midweek; book by phone.

venues.name: Spill the Beans
venues.note: Small, cheerful coffee shop on Castle Street on the left bank: excellent lattes and mochas, cinnamon rolls, toasties, sandwiches, scones and croissants; dog-friendly. Notably kind, helpful staff.

venues.name: The Silver Oak
venues.note: Long-established Indian restaurant, quiet and comfortable, with authentic, fragrant cooking and generous portions: paneer butter masala, lamb masala, chicken tikka, peshwari naan. Friendly staff; vegan options handled well.

venues.name: Lord Bellamys
venues.note: Pub: welcoming town pub on Northgate Street, good for a party, with live music at events. Reviewers say it serves food: grilled fish specials and seafood pasta, coeliac-friendly. Times and menu not published.

venues.name: 1810 Steakhouse
venues.note: Argentinian-style steakhouse, among the best steaks around, reviewers say: tomahawk for two, T-bone, striploin, halibut, provoleta, bone-marrow mash and chimichurri; desserts praised. Higher-priced; book.

venues.name: Garrison Coffee Co
venues.note: Cosy, roomy coffee shop on Church Street, named among Ireland's top 20 coffee shops two years running (its own Instagram), with a corner for dogs: good coffee, matcha, açaí bowls, home-made soup, croissants and sweet treats. Service has the odd off day.

venues.name: Loaves and Fishes
venues.note: Café and deli in the Left Bank Mall near Sean's Bar, much recommended for breakfast and lunch: the breakfast bap, seafood chowder with brown bread, burgers, ciabattas and an Irish cheese steak. Warm, attentive service.

venues.name: Biddy O'Dowd's
venues.note: Lively, friendly pub on Mardyke Street: an excellent pint of Guinness, good cocktails, a blazing fire and locals who welcome visitors. No food described.

venues.name: Nuts Corner
venues.note: Pub: drinks only, no food. Small, traditional bar with horse racing on the television and music some nights. Popular with locals.

venues.name: The Fiddlers
venues.note: Pub: drinks only, no food. Small, genuinely local pub on O'Connell Street with a pool table, a great pint and an owner, staff and regulars who make visitors feel at home; many prefer it to Sean's.

venues.name: Harvest Homemade
venues.note: Café and takeaway in Athlone Town Centre: full breakfasts, baps, wraps, focaccia, toasties, desserts and mochas. Friendly service; the food gets mixed reviews.

venues.name: O'Brien's Pub
venues.note: Pub: proper old Irish pub on Mardyke Street, full of antiques, with a friendly welcome, a great pint and a big beer garden with pool and darts. Reviewers mention offers on cocktails and toasties; no meals described.

venues.name: Savoury Fare
venues.note: Busy, cosy café on the first floor of Irishtown Central: breakfast baps, paninis, BLTs, a hot lunch daily from midday, carrot cake and very good coffee; best gluten-free choice in town, one reviewer says. Rolls, wraps, salads and soups all day. Its own site gives Monday to Saturday 09:30–17:30 and Sunday 10:30–17:30 for Fernhill, which differs from the hours shown here.

venues.name: Grind & Dose (train station)
venues.note: Coffee kiosk in the railway station: excellent coffee, pastries, brownies and filled croissants; friendly baristas. Pastries can sell out.

venues.name: The Dark Horse Bar & Kitchen
venues.note: Gastropub with an upstairs of pool tables and darts: big portions at fair prices. Known for its burgers (the Cheese Please), garlic cheese fries, a huge Guinness beef stew, fish and chips and good cocktails; friendly, efficient service.
